ai.summary: A real native <select>, visibly: submits through a plain form, validates natively, and the popup is the browser's own.
whenToUse: The value is one of a fixed set of choices
The form must submit through plain HTML with no component state reading
The list is long enough that radio buttons would be a wall
whenNotToUse: The choice is between two options — use a Switch or two Radio Buttons; a select hides the answer
The options depend on typing — use a Combobox
There are fewer than five options and the page has room — Radio Group shows every answer at once
ai.accessibility: Renders a real native `<select>`, visibly — §4's hidden-native path was rejected deliberately, so the popup is the browser's: touch, wheel, typeahead, and native validation all work without a listbox reimplementing them. FACE with all three form callbacks; `required` is enforced by the browser and never suppressed; the label is associated through `for`, and an error sets `aria-invalid` with an icon beside its text, never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). `sk-value-change` fires only for user-initiated changes. Options are JSON, because slot distribution cannot move host children into the render tree.
ai.example: <sk-select name="environment" label="Environment" required placeholder="Choose an environment" options='[{"value":"production","label":"Production"}]'></sk-select>
knownLimitations: The popup cannot be styled — that is the trade the visible-native decision makes, and it is why the popup works everywhere
Options are JSON, not slotted markup — slot distribution cannot reach the render tree
SSR consumers must pass an explicit `id` for a separately-rendered `Label` to find it (section 4, forms contract)
